name: Definition

candidate_lineage.non_effect: Successor lineage does not supersede, withdraw, or admit candidate.1.

bootstrap.effect: The Artifact Type/v1 bootstrap root and seven supporting Foundation types are admitted for the exact scope of CAL-DECISION-0013-FOUNDATION-01-ADMISSION. Definition/v1 may now be evaluated as a promotion candidate, but this candidate is not admitted.

producer_constraints: Create or revise a Definition only through an owner-authorized definitions-governance process.
Assign a stable definition identifier and explicit semantic owner.
Colocate scientific/formal, plain-language, and CyberAlchemy Lab domain-context voices.
Treat only the scientific/formal voice as normative; interpretive voices must declare normative=false.
Bind every external source to its exact admitted selector, target use, and source-admission decision; admission of selected bytes does not import the full legacy source or status.
Prepare the Definition candidate together with registry, generated index, and drift-audit postimages before requesting canonical promotion.
Generate every DEFINITION.md from definition.json and reject exact-byte projection drift.
Create a new candidate epoch whenever any admission-bound Definition/v1 artifact-type byte changes.
origin_constraints: Directory placement does not establish type, origin, ownership, authority, lifecycle, or bounded-context identity.
The admitted owner registry resolves accountable principals, but each role retains its separate scope and decision obligations.
Schema PASS, projection parity, or a validation receipt proves only the checks named by that receipt.
An admitted source selector supplies bounded evidence; only a Definition promotion decision can make a Lab term canonical.

projection_contract.determinism_contract: Two renders of identical canonical JSON bytes must produce identical UTF-8 Markdown bytes ending in one newline.

four_facets.classification: The candidate separately declares artifact type, semantic kind, authority kind, lifecycle posture, and successor lineage.
four_facets.schema: The unchanged closed Definition/v1 instance schema is bound by exact digest; candidate.2 changes prerequisite and governance bindings, not the instance shape.
four_facets.human_continuation: ARTIFACT.md is regenerated from this machine record and exposes resolved prerequisites, remaining residue, and the separate promotion route.
four_facets.machine_checkable: The candidate validator checks predecessor immutability, Foundation admission, owner/profile/source bindings, refreshed drift evidence, fixtures, and deterministic projection.

definition_semantics.scientific_formal_voice: A Definition is a versioned, owner-scoped semantic artifact that assigns a term its normative meaning within an exact authority scope. It is structurally complete only when stable identity, applicability, exclusions, a scientific/formal normative voice, explicitly non-normative plain-language and domain-context voices, boundaries, admitted source posture, primary consumers, a synchronized registry postimage, generated index, and a current drift route are declared. Only a separate owner promotion decision can make an exact Definition version canonical authority.
definition_semantics.formal_model: DefinitionComplete(d) iff stable_identity(d) and exact_scope(d) and formal_voice(d) and nonnormative_plain_voice(d) and nonnormative_domain_voice(d) and boundaries(d) and admitted_sources(d) and registry_postimage(d) and generated_index(d) and current_drift_route(d). DefinitionComplete(d) does not imply admitted(d), canonical_authority(d), correct(d), or implemented(d).
definition_semantics.plain_language_voice: A Definition is the project-owned record that says exactly what a term means, where that meaning applies, how people can understand it, and how later drift will be challenged. Even a complete, passing candidate does not count as canonical until its owner promotes it.
definition_semantics.domain_context_voice: In CyberAlchemy Lab, Definition/v1 candidate.2 is the successor artifact-type proposal built after Foundation-01 admission. Machine JSON owns every record, Markdown is generated, the three legacy CyberAlchemy-v2 selectors are bounded admitted inputs, the canonical registry remains empty, and Product or Governance placement never implies a bounded context.
boundaries: A glossary hint, source quotation, research finding, ontology node, generated index row, or narrative explanation is not a Definition by itself.
Plain-language and domain-context voices may explain but cannot weaken or expand the scientific/formal voice.
Definition identity, artifact type, semantic kind, authority kind, lifecycle posture, owner scope, and bounded-context membership are independent axes.
Schema validity proves representation shape only; it does not prove semantic truth, promotion, conformance, or implementation.
Admitting Definition/v1 would admit the artifact-type contract only; it would not automatically admit the term Definition or any Definition instance.
